definitions.explanation: The act of both parties moving toward each other's position to reach an agreement. Emphasizes mutual effort and willingness to find common ground.

examples.japanese: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りの{姿勢|しせい}を{見|み}せる
examples.english: to show a willingness to compromise

examples.japanese: {双方|そうほう}の{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Compromise from both sides is necessary.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{対立|たいりつ}を{終|お}わらせるため、{両国|りょうこく}が{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りを{見|み}せた。
examples.english: Both countries showed a willingness to compromise in order to end years of conflict.

notes:
USAGE: Often used in expressions like {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りを{見|み}せる (to show willingness to compromise) or {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りがある (there is compromise). The related verb {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}る means "to approach" or "to compromise."

NUANCE: {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}り emphasizes the mutual nature of compromise—both parties meeting in the middle rather than one side simply giving in. It has a positive connotation of cooperation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りの{姿勢|しせい} (attitude of compromise)
- {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りを{見|み}せる (to show willingness to compromise)
- {相互|そうご}の{歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}り (mutual compromise)
- {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}りがない (no willingness to compromise)

RELATED WORDS:
- {譲歩|じょうほ} (concession - more one-sided)
- {妥協|だきょう} (compromise - more general)
- {折|お}り{合|あ}い (compromise, settlement)
